rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2<U+2013>2.3 <U+2014> continuous eddy-covariance measurements of carbon and water fluxes at the Daman maize site 2012<U+2013>2018, with soil moisture, lysimeter and isotope data. Q2: Section 3.2, Table 2, Figure 7 <U+2014> annual ET fell from 733 to 640 kg H2O m<U+2212>2 (<U+2212>13%) and ecosystem/canopy WUE rose 9<U+2013>14% / 11% after the site switched from flood to drip irrigation in 2017; Section 4.2 states drip irrigation significantly saves water in oasis agriculture. Q4: Table 2 and Figure 5/7 <U+2014> ET partitioned into T and E with soil evaporation falling ~20% and T 11<U+2013>14% under drip; soil moisture at 4, 40 and 160 cm measured and shown to drop 27<U+2013>32% (shallow) and 36<U+2013>42% (deep), indicating reduced deep percolation (Section 4.2). Q8: Section 2.2 and Table 2 caption <U+2014> authors note drip intensity and frequency were higher in 2017 than 2018, so they report effects both from 2018 alone and the 2017<U+2013>2018 average, giving ranges; Section 2.6 notes lysimeter/isotope validation data exist only for the 2012 growing season.
rows.notes: Single-site before/after comparison (flood 2012<U+2013>2016 vs drip 2017<U+2013>2018) rather than a side-by-side trial; plastic film mulch was present in both periods, so the comparison isolates irrigation method. Q3 'no': the WUE/ET effect rests on one method (eddy covariance GPP/ET); the lysimeter and isotope data only validate the ET partitioning model in 2012 and are not an independent estimate of the drip effect. Q7 'no': authors describe drip as 'deficient amount and higher frequency' under film mulch but do not state these as required conditions. Q8 borderline: the caveat about varying drip intensity across years is a stated data restriction. Q9 'no': the 9<U+2013>14% range reflects two alternative data selections (2018 vs 2017<U+2013>2018 mean), not a dispersion measure; the <U+00B1> values given are for multi-year means of WUE and climate variables, not for the drip-vs-flood difference.

notes: Full text appears complete, though some figure captions and paragraphs are duplicated from PDF layout. Study is a single flux-tower site (seed maize, Zhangye, Heihe River Basin) with an irrigation-practice change in 2017 used as a natural before/after comparison.
